entries.note: Abstract quote verbatim (PMID 19608418). Amira tricyclics are class proxies; untested correct. Whether an in-vitro human whole-blood assay is a 'preclinical model' under the brief is a rule question, not a drafting error.

Abstract quote verbatim; JACI paywalled. NCT01007721 no results. Same assay ex vivo on dosed patients showed dose-related block, so same holds weakly; source never states in-vitro potency beside it. No preclinical BI 671800 shape-change paper on PubMed; product_in_model null stands.

Full-text quote verbatim (PMC5379543); status/year stand. Underlying model is Krause 2016 Clin Pharmacokinet (doi 10.1007/s40262-015-0354-3, epub 2015), which set the 90%-trough-blockade target: model_first_use_year 2017->2016 and add a 2016 untested opener.

Abstract quote verbatim. Mouse model used only for Amira/Array proxies; untested correct. Kupczyk 2017 review (PMID 28612233) asserts an animal-vs-clinic discrepancy in AR but is a review, not a source; no primary comparison exists.
Abstract-only quote verbatim (conclusion sentence). NCT01448902 start 2007-03, n=36, no results posted; model_first_use_year 2007 checks. No field trial of OC000459 in rhinitis, so untested is right.

Quotes verbatim (full text), but Ratner never compares chamber with the Phase 3 null (blames exposure/dose, 'not fully known'); setipiprant never ran in the chamber. Only source-stated model-vs-field comparison is Phase 2 'in line with' chamber trials: same.

Empty list. Rule 6 wants an untested opener at the model's first-use year; empty only when no model exists. No source names a setipiprant tox model: Fretz 2013 abstract = rat/dog PK + in-vitro ADME (full text 403); Ratner silent.

missing: dose: 2016 `untested` opener on Krause 2016, Clin Pharmacokinet 35:1-13 (https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-015-0354-3, epub 2015, NCT? none in abstract): PK/PD model of CRTH2 internalization that set 'Ninety percent of maximum blockade of CRTH2 internalization at trough' as the PD target; it is the modelling study Ratner 2017 cites post hoc. model_first_use_year on the 2017 entry becomes 2016.

efficacy 2017: if the re-scorer keeps `same`, the quote must change to Ratner's Discussion sentence 'This is in line with the growing clinical evidence from several CRHT2 antagonists investigated in allergen challenge trials supporting the therapeutic role of CRTH2 antagonism in the treatment of AR' (verbatim, incl. the CRHT2 typo), with comparison_stated true, subjects patients, product_in_model false, magnitude direction_only, source_calls_it match; the Phase 3 null (-0.02, p=0.652, NCT01484119, cetirizine positive) stays in note/judgement as an unadjudicated contradiction.

safety: no source in hand names the tox model. Fretz 2013 (10.1021/jm400122f) abstract names only rat/dog PK and in-vitro ADME (ACS full text 403); Ratner 2017 says 'no safety issues were identified' with no model; Aissaoui 2023 (10.1002/cmdc.202300007) cites an unnamed 'safety issue as observed in non-clinical studies' for follow-up ACT-453859, not setipiprant. Either keep the cell empty and say in the context note that the tox package is unsourced, or open it `untested` 2013 on Fretz if its full text names the species.
rule_questions: Does 'model' include human experimental systems? Three of the four cells here rest on an in-vitro human whole-blood assay, a human allergen-challenge chamber and a clinical PK-PD occupancy model; the brief says 'preclinical models' but also 'the model the class actually relied on'. If excluded, this context collapses to the mouse rhinitis model (untested) and nothing else.

efficacy 2017: can a drafter-juxtaposed contradiction be `contra`? Rule 1 requires the source to make the comparison; Ratner never puts the chamber beside the Phase 3 null and setipiprant was never dosed in the chamber (the brief allows class proxies via product_in_model=false, so that alone does not bar it). Under the rules as written the supportable status is `same` on the Phase 2 comparison Ratner does state; `contra` only if juxtaposition is admitted, in which case it overrides. `untested` is wrong because a comparison was published.

engagement 2014: does an ex vivo PD readout in the same assay as the model count as a 'published comparison' when the source never places the in-vitro potency beside it (comparison_stated false)? If not, engagement 2014 -> untested.

dose 2017: is Ratner's post hoc occupancy explanation ('might also partly explain') a `same` comparison (model: <30% at target -> borderline; patients: borderline/null) or `untested` as drafted? The brief does not say whether post hoc counts.

safety: when the tox package certainly exists (drug reached Phase 3) but no source names the model, is the cell empty (as drafted) or does rule 6 require an `untested` opener with 'model unsourced' in the note?

Kupczyk 2017 (PMID 28612233, Drugs, article type Review) appears in no src/srcLabel field of the draft; it can only have been a pointer.
